candidates.name: Cathedral
candidates.content: The view from the tower over the old town and the Rio Formosa is a highlight.

candidates.name: Roman Ruins of Milreu
candidates.content: A luxurious Roman villa that evolved into a Christian basilica by the 4th century. Notable features include well-preserved mosaic floors with marine motifs, remnants of thermal baths, a temple, and agricultural installations, offe

candidates.name: Estoi Palace
candidates.content: Renowned for its blend of architectural styles, including Baroque, Rococo, Neoclassical, and Romantic elements. The palace was constructed in the 19th century, and was completed in 1909 under the ownership of José Francisco da Sil

candidates.name: Bone Chapel
candidates.alt: Capela dos Ossos (inside Igreja do Carmo)
candidates.content: This chapel is almost completely made of bones taken from a former monk graveyard.

candidates.name: Old town
candidates.content: A well-preserved section of town off the harbour with cobblestone streets and 18th century Portuguese and Moorish-influenced architecture. It is a great place for a peaceful and almost private walk back in time in an area that has

candidates.name: Ria Formosa National Park
candidates.content: In Faro and Olhão you can take a boat trip, birdwatching tours, kayaking or other eco tours and other activities to discover the nature and wildlife of this natural park. Several companies offer packages and tours. Ask at the tour

candidates.name: Faro Jewish Heritage Centre
candidates.content: Established in 1851, the Faro Jewish Cemetery is the only remaining vestige of the first post-Inquisition Jewish presence in Portugal. It served as a burial place for a thriving 60 family community (also known as "Little Jerusalem

candidates.name: Faro beach
candidates.content: This beach is several kilometres long and so normally never gets crowded, even in the height of summer. Most of the beach is gently sloping though it can take a sudden dip in places. There are the usual beach-side stalls and a pub

candidates.name: SC Farense
candidates.content: The "Lions of Faro" were relegated in 2025 and now play soccer in Liga 2, the second tier. Their home ground Estádio de São Luís (capacity 7000) is 1 km northeast of city centre.

candidates.name: Bar CheSsenta
candidates.content: Decorated with many photos of Che Guevara and attracts a 20s-30s crowd with reasonably priced drinks. They do karaoke on some nights also.

candidates.name: Restaurante Travessa
candidates.price: €11 for the menu of the day
candidates.content: Despite being identified as "tapas" the servings are generous. Good variety of dishes.

candidates.name: Snackbar El Sombrero
candidates.content: Simple pleasant cuisine right next to the bus station.

candidates.name: Restaurante Sal e Pimenta
candidates.content: Hidden spot with good homemade food, generous portions and a family vibe.

candidates.name: Miminhos Caseiros
candidates.content: Authentic local cuisine with a friendly and passionate owner.

candidates.name: Namastey
candidates.content: Indian food. Friendly staff.

candidates.name: Tasquinha Cruzeiro
candidates.content: The fried calamari of this local cuisine are nice. The service is very gracious.

candidates.name: A Venda
candidates.content: Portuguese tapas. Very vegetarian friendly. Good wine selection.

candidates.name: 100 Montaditos Faro
candidates.content: Tapas restaurant with a good atmosphore and nice outdoor seating.

candidates.name: Chalet restaurante
candidates.content: An Asian restaurant that offers a wide variety of fresh sushi. Very friendly owners and employees.

candidates.name: Le Marquis
candidates.content: In a wonderful building. The decor has a traditional style.

candidates.name: Modesto Tavern
candidates.content: Very good fish and octopus cataplana.

candidates.name: Restaurante Alameda
candidates.content: Original recipes.

candidates.name: Faro Municipal Market
candidates.content: Mid-size farmers' market with the usual local fare and a rather wide selection. A supermarket in an underground floor and a few restaurants and cafès in the same building.

candidates.name: Forum Algarve
candidates.content: A shopping mall built around a large couryard with a fountain; business-wise it has about 100 stores, hypermarket, a 5-screen multiplex cinema, a food court, and convenience services.

december.text: Faro beach (Praia de Faro) on a narrow peninsula by the airport. Large number of departures during high season, from 29 October to 31 December 5 times daily. Adult €2.15/€3.75 one-way/return.
